title: Battle of Chaeronea
summary: In August 338 BC, near Chaeronea in Boeotia, Philip II of Macedon defeated an alliance of Greek city-states led by Athens and Thebes. The allied line broke and fled, ending effective resistance. Philip then imposed a settlement, the League of Corinth, and Macedonian dominance in Greece began.

as_recorded.value: the Battle of Chaeronea did not occur until August 338 BC

importance.justification: Decisive battle that ended Greek city-state resistance and established Macedonian hegemony over Greece.

audience_note: Describes battle deaths, including the annihilation of the Sacred Band of Thebes.

sources.title: Battle of Chaeronea | History, Interpretations, & Facts | Britannica

reviewer_note: Both sources give August 338 BC, so the year is -337 astronomically; Wikidata's month matches. Sources differ in interpretation of the tactics (feigned retreat versus plain phalanx fight), which the summary leaves out. Exact site coordinates are not given, so the uncertainty is approximate.
